notes: COLD scan. Primary lead (BatchNFTMinter unguarded reentrancy) rigorously adjudicated NON-exploitable with traces. Leads 2/3/4 confirmed non-issues. Lead 5 (stakedId parity) yields one Low footgun in InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator plus a QA note on NFTStakerMigrator. Known-intentional designs (emergencyWithdraw skip-sync, empty-pool guards, APY-as-floor, window-restart-on-inflow) NOT re-flagged; window-restart griefing deferred to econ-scanner.

findings.description: [PRIMARY LEAD] batchMint has no ReentrancyGuard and calls tokenMinter.mint() in a loop; NFTMinterV2._executeMint does `_mint(recipient,...)` which fires onERC1155Received on the caller-supplied recipient (attacker-controlled) mid-loop, while the contract holds pulled paymentToken, a live max approval to the minter, and a pre-loop nudge-pot snapshot. Verified against NFTMinterV2._executeMint control flow.
findings.adjudication: SELF-DEFEATING / non-exploitable on every vector examined. (1) DOUBLE-COLLECT: outer snapshots nudge pot P before loop; a reentrant inner frame with count>=nudgeSize also snapshots P and pays P to recipient (line 295). When control returns, the outer frame's stale snapshot transfer of P (line 295) reverts because the pot is now empty -> whole tx reverts. To let the outer survive, outer must have snapshot 0 (count<nudgeSize), i.e. it does NOT collect -> only one collection total. (2) COST-SHORTCUT: collecting P always requires the collecting frame to complete count>=nudgeSize REAL mints, each paying the ramping dispatcher price; no frame can qualify for less. (3) APPROVAL: inner frame's forceApprove(minter,0) at line 284 revokes the outer's allowance, so any outer loop iteration after the reentry reverts inside _executeMint's safeTransferFrom -> tx reverts (unless reentry is the last iteration, which reduces to case 1/2). (4) REFUND-SWEEP THEFT: an inner frame's end-of-call full-balance refund (line 301) would sweep the outer frame's unspent payment, BUT the reentry only fires on the recipient the OUTER CALLER chose. An attacker can only be the reentry point by being the recipient, i.e. by being the caller -> outer and inner msg.sender are the same attacker -> no victim funds exist to steal; funds swept are the attacker's own. There is no path for an attacker to inject their malicious recipient into a third party's batchMint. Nudge pot P is externally-funded and can be extracted at most once, at full mint cost. NO profit, NO theft, NO double-collect.
findings.attackVector: None realizable. Requires attacker to control the mint recipient, which means attacker is also the caller (single-party); nested frames cannot over-extract the fixed pot or the caller's own funds.
findings.recommendation: Add OZ ReentrancyGuard (nonReentrant) to batchMint as cheap defense-in-depth and future-proofing against config changes (e.g. if nudge logic ever gains cross-call shared state or a persistent per-caller ledger). Not a current vulnerability.

findings.description: [LEAD 2] Static flagged that an earlier modifier's external call could reenter before nonReentrant arms. migrateOut(:152) and migrateIn(:186) are `external onlyOwner nonReentrant` (onlyOwner precedes nonReentrant).
findings.adjudication: No pre-guard external call exists. Ownable's onlyOwner -> _checkOwner() is an internal view (storage read of owner() + compare); it performs zero external calls, so there is no reentry window before the ReentrancyGuard sets its slot. Additionally both functions are onlyOwner, so any reentry would require the trusted owner. False positive.

findings.description: [LEAD 3] `nftMinter.mint(_dispatcherIndex, recipient)` return bool is ignored, raising the question of a silent mint/nudge accounting mismatch.
findings.adjudication: No mismatch possible. NFTMinterV2.mint/_executeMint either returns `true` after minting exactly 1 unit, or REVERTS (require on paused/registered/disabled, and safeTransferFrom on insufficient payment/allowance). It never returns false. Any failed mint reverts the whole batch atomically. Therefore `count` iterations always equal `count` real mints, and the nudge payout gates on `count` (not on a success tally), so ignoring the bool changes nothing. Safe.

findings.description: [LEAD 4] _syncBudget calls dispatcherHook.pull(); UniboostMintDebtHook.pull() is onlyOwnerOrRecipient (hook :141). If this staker is neither the hook owner nor its `recipient`, pull() reverts, bricking stake/unstake/claim and initiateMigration.
findings.adjudication: Real but bounded and already documented. (a) The requirement 'staker must be hook.recipient' is stated in the staker NatSpec (:105-108), the profile trust assumptions, and the divergence map -> an OBVIOUS, documented operational precondition (Law 3: obvious owner-config, not a reportable footgun). (b) Principal is NEVER trapped: emergencyWithdraw() (:622) takes NO _syncBudget/pull path and is callable while paused, so every staker can always exit with principal even if the hook is mis-wired or permanently broken. userMigrate() escapes pull() too, though it needs Migrating state (which initiateMigration -> pull() must set, so the guaranteed universal escape is emergencyWithdraw). Verified emergencyWithdraw and _exitPosition/_safePayTo make no pull() call. No fund loss; DoS is recoverable and gated behind a documented wiring step.

findings.description: [LEAD 5] The migrator's `stakedId` is an immutable constructor param (:53, :107) with NO on-chain assertion that it equals the staker's live `stakedId` (the INFTStakerMigratable interface does not even expose a stakedId getter). migrateOut parks whatever id the staker's batchMigrate transfers (staker.stakedId), and depositFor/migrateIn pull staker.stakedId back out (all id-driven by the staker, and setApprovalForAll grants all ids). But claimTimedOut (:254) and rescueERC1155 (:281-288) transfer/guard using the migrator's OWN immutable stakedId. If those ever diverge from the actually-parked id, two silent breakages occur.
findings.attackVector: Divergence is reachable without malice: the staker's stakedId is owner-mutable via setStakedId while totalStaked==0 (the documented 'NFT reissued under a new ID' path). If the staker's stakedId is changed after the migrator is deployed (immutable stakedId goes stale), then for stake parked under the new id Z while migrator.stakedId==X!=Z: (1) claimTimedOut reverts (migrator holds 0 of id X) -> the permissionless self-escape hatch is DEAD, users depend entirely on the trusted operator's migrateIn; (2) rescueERC1155(Z, ...) takes the ELSE branch (Z != migrator.stakedId) and sweeps the full balance of Z with NO totalParked floor check -> the deliberately-designed 'parked principal untouchable even against the owner' guarantee (the whole point of the floor at :283-286) is silently voided. rescueERC1155(X,...) instead underflows (balance 0 - totalParked) and safe-reverts.
findings.adjudication: Non-obvious footgun (Law 3 in-scope): a stakedId mismatch, most plausibly from a legitimate setStakedId reconfiguration between migrator deployment and use, silently disables the escape hatch and removes the parked-principal floor. Owner is trusted for knowing actions, but the floor is a guardrail explicitly designed to protect parked stake 'even against the owner' (per NatSpec :275-276) and its silent defeat is a surprising consequence, not an obvious one. No direct theft path (rescue is onlyOwner), so bounded to Low. Requires a config/misuse trigger; the InPlace migrator's stated use case is dispatcher/hook rewire (not stakedId change), but nothing on-chain prevents the divergence.
findings.recommendation: Add a stakedId() getter to INFTStakerMigratable and assert `_stakedId == staker.stakedId()` in the constructor, OR derive the id from the staker at call time instead of storing an immutable copy. At minimum document that the InPlace migrator must be redeployed if the staker's stakedId ever changes.

findings.description: [LEAD 5 cont'd] NFTStakerMigrator stores immutable `stakedId` (:44) and asserts oldStaker!=newStaker and non-zero addresses, but never asserts oldStaker.stakedId == newStaker.stakedId == this.stakedId, and its own `stakedId` immutable is NEVER referenced inside migrate() (migrate uses setApprovalForAll for all ids and delegates the concrete id to each staker).
findings.adjudication: No value can be misrouted or stranded. If oldStaker.stakedId != newStaker.stakedId, batchMigrate transfers the old id into the migrator, then the FIRST newStaker.depositFor pulls the new id which the migrator does not hold -> ERC1155 insufficient-balance revert -> the entire migrate() (including the batchMigrate settle/mint/zeroing) rolls back atomically. So a mismatch is a hard DoS with clean rollback, not a fund-loss. The unused `stakedId` immutable is misleading (implies a parity guarantee it never enforces).
findings.recommendation: Remove the unused immutable or wire it into an explicit constructor-time parity assertion (needs a stakedId() getter on the interface). QA/hardening only.

clearedChecklist.classicSingleFnReentrancy: batchMint adjudicated non-exploitable (CODE-001); stakers' stake/unstake/claim/emergencyWithdraw/userMigrate/batchMigrate/depositFor all nonReentrant with strict CEI (state mutated before every ERC1155/ERC20 out-transfer).
clearedChecklist.crossContractReentrancy: Migrator<->staker loops (batchMigrate/depositFor) and BatchNFTMinter<->NFTMinterV2 examined; migrators are onlyOwner+nonReentrant, staker legs nonReentrant. No A->B->A state-desync path found.
clearedChecklist.crossFunctionReentrancy: Staker guards are contract-wide OZ ReentrancyGuard (shared lock across stake/unstake/claim/migrate), so sibling reentry is blocked.
clearedChecklist.readOnlyReentrancy: Staker views (pendingReward/totalBudget/totalDebt/runwaySeconds/currentRewardRate) could be consumed by an integrator, but every state-changing exit updates accounting BEFORE the ERC1155 callback (CEI) and is nonReentrant, so no transient-inconsistent window is exposed to a callback. No downstream oracle-style consumer identified in scope.
clearedChecklist.erc1155ReceiveHook: onERC1155Received fires on mint recipient (BatchNFTMinter path, CODE-001 non-exploitable) and on ERC1155 out-transfers in stakers (all nonReentrant + CEI). Migrator/staker are ERC1155Holder (inbound hooks return selector, no reentry).
clearedChecklist.erc777: N/A - reward token is phUSD (mintable ERC20), stake token is ERC1155; no ERC777 hooks in scope.
